pages.title: Employment Verification Letter
pages.description: Create a clear employment verification letter with the fields, employer version, employee request, checklist, and source-backed boundaries a reviewer may need.
pages.summary: An employment verification letter confirms factual employment details. The exact fields depend on the requester and the employer’s disclosure policy.
pages.primaryCta: Use the free Letter Writing Studio
keyFacts: Use the employer’s official letterhead or authorized verification system when available.
Confirm only facts the employer is permitted and willing to disclose.
Match the requester’s instructions; some need dates and title, while others also request current status or pay information.
Never invent employment, income, dates, titles, signatures, or contact details.
fields: Employer legal name and contact information
Compensation only when authorized and requested
Authorized verifier name, title, signature, and date
steps: Ask the requester exactly which fields and format it accepts.
Ask HR or the authorized employer representative how verification is handled.
Gather the employee’s correct name, title, dates, and any consent form.
Draft or request a concise verification using only authorized facts.
Check every date, amount, and contact detail against employer records.
Send through the channel the requester specified and save a copy.
pages.template:
[Employer letterhead]

[Date]

To whom it may concern:

This letter confirms that [Employee full name] is/was employed by [Employer legal name] as [Job title]. [Employee name] began employment on [Start date]. [Current status or end date, if authorized and requested].

[Optional compensation sentence only if authorized and requested: The employee’s current compensation is [amount and pay frequency].]

For questions about this verification, contact [Authorized verifier name/title] at [official phone/email].

Sincerely,
[Authorized verifier name]
[Title]
[Employer legal name]
pages.alternateTemplate:
Subject: Employment verification request

Hello [HR or verifier name],

Please provide an employment verification for [requester/purpose]. The requester asks for: [list required fields]. Their preferred delivery method is [method], and the deadline is [date].

I authorize release of the requested employment information to [requester] as permitted by company policy. Please tell me if you need a signed consent form or any additional details.

Thank you,
[Employee name]
[Employee ID, if appropriate]
mistakes: Using a personal email or unverifiable contact when an official channel is available.
Adding performance opinions, reasons for separation, or sensitive details that were not requested.
Including salary without authorization.
Letting dates, title, status, or pay frequency conflict with records.
Treating a self-written statement as employer verification when the requester requires third-party confirmation.

faq.question: What is an employment verification letter?
faq.answer: It is a factual confirmation of employment details such as employer, job title, dates, and current status. The requester and employer policy determine the accepted fields and delivery method.

faq.question: Does it need salary information?
faq.answer: Not always. Include compensation only when the requester requires it and the employer is authorized to disclose it.

faq.question: Can an employee write the letter?
faq.answer: An employee can request or draft a proposed version, but a requester may require verification from HR, a supervisor, payroll, or an authorized verification service.

faq.question: What if the employer uses an automated verification service?
faq.answer: Follow that process. A platform-generated verification may be more acceptable than a manually signed letter.

faq.question: Does a verification letter guarantee approval?
faq.answer: No. It confirms facts; it does not control a landlord, lender, employer, agency, or other reviewer’s decision.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Labor — Employment Verification
Defense Finance and Accounting Service — Civilian Employment Verification

pages.boundary: ApprovalPrep does not verify employment, contact employers, create employer signatures, or create fake employment or income records. You or the authorized employer sends the final verification.

pages.title: 609 Dispute Letter: What Section 609 Does—and Does Not—Do
pages.description: Use a source-backed 609 letter template while understanding the difference between FCRA disclosure rights and the credit-report dispute process.
pages.summary: Section 609 of the Fair Credit Reporting Act concerns disclosure of information in a consumer’s file. The reinvestigation procedure for disputed credit-report information is addressed in Section 611.
keyFacts: A “609 letter” does not create an automatic deletion right or loophole.
Ask for your consumer-file disclosures when you need to see what a reporting company maintains about you.
Use a dispute process when specific information is inaccurate or incomplete.
Identify each disputed item and attach copies of supporting records; keep originals.
fields: Your full name and current address
Specific factual error or disclosure request
Copies of identity/address documents when required
Copies of records supporting the request
steps: Get and review your current credit reports.
Separate a file-disclosure request from a factual dispute.
List each specific item and explain what is inaccurate, incomplete, or missing.
Attach copies of supporting records and redact unrelated sensitive information.
Send through the reporting company’s accepted channel and keep proof.
Review the response and updated report before deciding the next step.
pages.templateTitle: File disclosure and dispute clarification template
pages.template:
[Your name]
[Your address]
[Date]

[Credit reporting company]
[Address]

Re: Consumer file disclosure / disputed information

I am requesting the information in my consumer file that I am entitled to receive and, where identified below, I am disputing specific information that I believe is inaccurate or incomplete.

Item: [Company/account/item]
Report reference: [Reference]
Issue: [Specific factual problem]
Supporting records: [List copies enclosed]
Requested action: [Provide the requested file disclosure and/or investigate the specific disputed information and report the result.]

Please send the response to the address above. I have enclosed copies, not originals, and I am keeping a complete copy of this request.

Sincerely,
[Name]
pages.alternateTemplate:
Disclosure request: use when you need the information maintained in your consumer file.

Dispute request: use when a specific item is inaccurate or incomplete. Identify the item, explain the factual problem, and attach support.

Do not claim that a creditor or reporting company must delete accurate information merely because a particular form letter was sent.
mistakes: Calling every request a dispute without identifying a specific factual error.
Sending a copied “loophole” letter that does not match your report.
Demanding deletion of accurate information.
Failing to attach support or identify the report item.
Sending original documents or unnecessary identity information.

faq.question: What does FCRA Section 609 cover?
faq.answer: It addresses disclosures a consumer reporting agency must provide about information in the consumer’s file, subject to the statute’s terms.

faq.question: Where is the credit-report dispute procedure?
faq.answer: The FCRA reinvestigation procedure for disputed information is in Section 611, codified at 15 U.S.C. § 1681i.

faq.question: Will a 609 letter delete accurate information?
faq.answer: No automatic deletion right follows from sending a form letter. Accurate negative information generally cannot be forced off a report simply because it is unfavorable.

faq.question: What should a factual dispute include?
faq.answer: Identify the item, explain the specific inaccuracy or incompleteness, and include copies of documents that support your position.

faq.question: Does ApprovalPrep dispute for me?
faq.answer: No. ApprovalPrep is a self-service preparation tool. You review and send your own materials.

sources.label: 15 U.S.C. § 1681i — Procedure in case of disputed accuracy
CFPB — Disputing errors on credit reports

pages.boundary: ApprovalPrep is not a credit repair organization and does not contact credit reporting companies, furnishers, or creditors for you. This page provides educational, self-service preparation only.

pages.title: Goodwill Letter to Remove a Late Payment
pages.description: Prepare a concise goodwill request asking a creditor to consider a discretionary late-payment adjustment without claiming a legal right to remove accurate information.
pages.summary: A goodwill letter is a courtesy request. It can explain an isolated late payment and ask a creditor to consider an adjustment, but the creditor is not required to grant it.
pages.primaryCta: Use the free Letter Writing Studio
keyFacts: Use a goodwill request only for truthful account history.
A creditor’s decision is discretionary.
Accurate negative information generally cannot be forced off a credit report just because you ask.
A short request with an account-specific timeline is stronger than a copied threat or legal claim.
fields: Date and amount of the late payment
steps: Confirm the reported payment history is accurate.
If it is inaccurate, use a factual dispute instead of a goodwill request.
Write a short account-specific timeline.
Explain what changed and how future payments are protected.
Ask respectfully for a one-time discretionary adjustment.
Send through an accepted channel and keep a copy.
pages.template:
[Your name]
[Address]
[Date]

[Creditor name]
[Address or secure-message channel]

Re: Goodwill request for account ending [last four digits]

I am writing about the late payment reported for [month/year]. The payment was late because [brief truthful explanation]. The account is now [current status], and I have taken these steps to prevent a repeat: [automatic payment, reminders, corrected bank information, or other truthful action].

I value my relationship with [creditor] and respectfully ask whether you would consider a one-time goodwill adjustment to the late-payment reporting. I understand that this is a discretionary request and that accurate reporting is not required to be changed merely because I ask.

Thank you for reviewing my request.

Sincerely,
[Name]
pages.alternateTitle: When not to use a goodwill letter
pages.alternateTemplate: Use a factual dispute when the late payment is inaccurate, belongs to someone else, reflects the wrong date or amount, or should not appear for another documented reason. Use a goodwill request only when the reporting is accurate and you are asking for discretionary consideration.
mistakes: Claiming the creditor is legally required to remove accurate reporting.
Disputing an accurate late payment as if it were an error.
Writing a long emotional story without a clear account timeline.
Threatening complaints or litigation in a courtesy request.
Sending the same generic letter repeatedly without new information.

faq.question: Is a goodwill adjustment guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. It is a discretionary courtesy decision by the creditor.

faq.question: What if the late payment is actually wrong?
faq.answer: Use the creditor and credit-report dispute channels for a specific factual error rather than framing it as goodwill.

faq.question: Should I admit the payment was late?
faq.answer: Use truthful, precise language. A goodwill request is generally for accurate history, so do not manufacture a dispute.

faq.question: What supporting documents help?
faq.answer: Only include records relevant to the explanation or corrective action, such as proof of a bank error or account setup. Do not overshare unrelated personal records.

faq.question: Can ApprovalPrep contact the creditor?
faq.answer: No. You review and send your own request.

sources.label: CFPB — Sample letters for credit-report disputes

pages.boundary: This is a courtesy-request template, not a promise of deletion or score improvement. ApprovalPrep does not provide credit repair services or act for you.

pages.title: Letter of Explanation for a Late Payment
pages.description: Write a factual late-payment explanation for a lender, landlord, or other reviewer with a clear timeline, supporting documents, and no approval promises.
pages.summary: A late-payment explanation should identify the payment, explain the specific cause, show what changed, and point to evidence without minimizing or exaggerating the facts.
keyFacts: Answer the reviewer’s exact question.
Use dates, amounts, and account identifiers that match records.
Distinguish an isolated event from an unresolved pattern only when the evidence supports that distinction.
Explain corrective steps without predicting the reviewer’s decision.
steps: Copy the reviewer’s request into your notes.
Build a short timeline from statements and receipts.
Identify the narrow cause without adding unrelated history.
Attach only records that support the explanation.
State the current status and prevention steps.
Review for consistency and send through the requested channel.
pages.template:
[Your name]
[Application or loan number]
[Date]

To [Reviewer name or department]:

I am responding to the request for an explanation of the late payment on [account] for [month/year]. The payment was due on [date] and was made on [date]. The delay occurred because [specific, truthful cause].

The account is now [current status]. I have taken the following steps to reduce the chance of another late payment: [specific steps]. I have attached [documents] to support the dates and circumstances described above.

Please let me know if another document or clarification is required.

Sincerely,
[Name]
pages.alternateTemplate: Possible support includes the relevant account statement, payment confirmation, bank notice, employer or benefits record, repair invoice, medical billing record, or other document that directly supports the stated timeline. Use copies and redact unrelated account information.
mistakes: Using vague phrases such as “things happened” without dates.
Blaming a third party without evidence.
Attaching a large volume of unrelated personal records.
Claiming the issue can never happen again.
Asking ApprovalPrep to submit or negotiate with the reviewer.

faq.question: How long should the explanation be?
faq.answer: Usually one focused page is easier to review, but follow the requester’s instructions.

faq.question: Should I include personal hardship details?
faq.answer: Include only the context needed to explain the payment and support the timeline. Avoid unnecessary sensitive detail.

faq.question: What if the payment was reported inaccurately?
faq.answer: A letter of explanation may answer an application question, but use the appropriate creditor or credit-report dispute process for a factual reporting error.

faq.question: Does an explanation guarantee approval?
faq.answer: No. It provides context; the reviewer applies its own criteria.

faq.question: Can I use this for a mortgage?
faq.answer: You can adapt the structure, but follow the lender’s exact request and ask what documents it requires.

sources.label: CFPB — Create a loan application packet

pages.title: Letter of Explanation for a Large Deposit
pages.description: Explain the source of a large bank deposit with a traceable timeline, supporting documents, and lender-specific follow-up questions.
pages.summary: A lender may ask for the source of a large deposit when reviewing assets. The accepted evidence depends on the transaction, account, loan program, and lender instructions.
keyFacts: Ask the lender which deposit, statement period, and evidence it needs.
Trace the funds from their source into the reviewed account.
Do not describe borrowed money, gifts, sales proceeds, transfers, payroll, refunds, or cash deposits inaccurately.
Use documents that form a readable chain rather than a pile of unrelated statements.
steps: Identify the exact deposit the lender flagged.
Classify the truthful source: transfer, gift, sale, payroll, refund, loan, cash, or other.
Gather the documents that trace the source and transfer.
Ask whether a lender form, donor statement, bill of sale, or additional statement is required.
Write a concise explanation that matches the documents.
Redact unrelated account information only when permitted and retain the full copy trail.
pages.template:
[Your name]
[Loan/application number]
[Date]

To [Lender or underwriter]:

I am responding to the request regarding the deposit of [amount] posted to [account description/last four digits] on [date]. The funds came from [specific source]. The transaction occurred as follows: [brief trace from origin to deposit].

I have attached [list documents] to show the source and movement of the funds. Please let me know if your review requires a specific form or another statement period.

Sincerely,
[Name]
pages.alternateTemplate:
Account transfer: statements showing the withdrawal and deposit.
Gift: lender-required gift documentation and evidence of transfer.
Asset sale: bill of sale, ownership evidence, and deposit record.
Payroll or bonus: pay record and account deposit.
Refund: issuer notice and deposit record.
Loan proceeds: loan documents and transfer record; disclose accurately and ask how the lender treats the obligation.
Cash: ask the lender what evidence, if any, it will accept.
mistakes: Calling a deposit “savings” when the money came from another source.
Submitting only the receiving statement without tracing the origin.
Creating or altering bank, gift, payroll, sale, or loan documents.
Assuming one lender’s documentation rule applies to another.
Hiding a new debt or borrowed source.

faq.question: What counts as a large deposit?
faq.answer: There is no single universal number for every application. The lender identifies the deposits it needs explained based on its review and applicable requirements.

faq.question: Do I need every bank statement?
faq.answer: Provide the periods and accounts the lender requests. Ask before sending extra sensitive records.

faq.question: How do I explain a transfer between my own accounts?
faq.answer: Show the outgoing transaction from the source account and the matching incoming deposit in the reviewed account.

faq.question: What about a cash deposit?
faq.answer: Tell the truth and ask what evidence the lender accepts. Do not create a false receipt or source story.

faq.question: Does a clean explanation guarantee the loan?
faq.answer: No. It only addresses one documentation question.

sources.label: CFPB — Submit documents and answer requests from the lender
